actions: Retried public artifact/reproduction resolution for Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 and exact-title/DOI searches. The version-of-record article still states that all simulation/analysis code is at that Zenodo DOI; current public search transport did not expose the record file list/checksums and no clear non-author rerun/failure report was established.

Recovered the exact published source equations for the direction RNN: 512-unit vanilla recurrent layer, tau=2 leaky ReLU recurrence, per-step layer normalization, linear readout, cross-entropy summed over time, Adam lr=1e-4, T=100 synthetic direction clips, 12 directions and Bernoulli input noise p=0.01.

Executed a new source-derived causal control at reduced scale using the published recurrence equations and T=100. Compared (A) per-step-supervised leaky LayerNorm RNN, which mirrors the paper's loss-over-time structure; (B) the same recurrent architecture trained only on the final time step as a generic-recurrence control; and (C) a nearly parameter-matched non-recurrent temporal-convolution primitive encoder.

Used three independent data/model seeds; 16x16 binary oriented moving-bar videos; 12 directions; 100 frames; center speed 0.04 pixel/frame; Bernoulli pixel noise p=0.01; 720 train and 360 test clips per seed. Recurrent models had 21,452 parameters; non-recurrent control had 21,368 parameters.

Applied the paper-text random-interpolation analogue by inserting one shuffled frame between every adjacent pair: concatenate the adjacent binary frames, shuffle all 512 pixel values, take one frame-sized 256-value slice, reshape and insert. Also tested 50% random frame dropout.

Measured off-trajectory hidden-state recovery by adding Gaussian hidden perturbations at t=50 and tracking RMS distance from the model's own clean trajectory for 30 subsequent clean steps, plus participation-ratio diagnostics on late hidden states.

public_sources.title: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation
source_facts: Methods Eq.1-2: tau=2 leaky ReLU recurrence followed by per-step normalization.
Methods Eq.3-5: linear readout and cross-entropy summed over all T time steps; Adam lr=1e-4; truncated BPTT.
Direction pretraining: T=100 moving-bar clips, 12 directions, Bernoulli noise p=0.01; published direction-manifold participation ratio about 2.11.
Published perturbation analysis reports contraction back toward the input-anchored manifold within roughly 5-10 steps.

Random interpolation: flatten/concatenate each adjacent frame pair, randomly shuffle to destroy spatial locality while preserving pixel-intensity statistics, reshape and insert stochastic content between the pair.

design.generic_rnn_control: cross-entropy at final time step only
design.random_interpolation: one shuffled frame inserted in every adjacent gap

hidden_perturbation_recovery.interpretation: Per-step-supervised recurrence consistently contracted perturbations for the full 30-step horizon; final-only recurrent controls often bottomed out and then stopped improving or drifted.

participation_ratio.interpretation: The reduced source-derived experiment did not reproduce the paper's near-2D ring geometry. The source-like RNN was somewhat lower-dimensional than final-only recurrence on all late hidden samples, but class-mean PR was not lower; therefore robustness cannot be attributed here to a reproduced 2D attractor manifold.

source_derived_ablation.interpretation: Loss-over-time/per-step primitive supervision materially changes recurrent dynamics: with nearly matched clean accuracy it improved source-like interpolation retention from about 59.5% to 89.3% and produced stronger long-horizon recovery after hidden perturbation. However, the parameter-matched non-recurrent temporal encoder retained about 88.2% under interpolation and 100% under 50% dropout while also achieving higher clean accuracy. Because the reduced RNNs did not reproduce the published PR~2.11 ring, this run supports 'distributed temporal supervision sculpts contractive recurrent dynamics' but does not establish that low-dimensional continuous-attractor geometry is the causal source of robustness or that recurrence beats a strong primitive-isolated feedforward control.
scope: Not an exact replication: the official Zenodo generator/code is still inaccessible, and this run used 64 recurrent units rather than 512 plus a source-derived 16x16 oriented moving-bar generator.
The publication trains up to 10^6 episodes on an A40; this run used far less optimization. Failure to reproduce PR~2.11 is therefore not evidence against the published geometry.

The final-only recurrent control intentionally changes the temporal loss while preserving the recurrent equations/parameter count; it isolates supervision distribution, not every other possible training difference.
The non-recurrent temporal-convolution control is an engineering comparator, not a source baseline, and has slightly higher clean accuracy.
Random-interpolation semantics follow the paper text but may differ from the exact Zenodo reshape/splitting implementation.

evidence_added_this_run: Three-seed reduced T=100 source-equation control: per-step-supervised RNN clean 93.80±3.36%, all-gap interpolation 83.70±1.28% (89.28±1.91% retention), 50% dropout 92.04±2.08% (98.16±1.66% retention).
Same-architecture final-only recurrent control clean 94.17±3.82% but interpolation 55.83±6.21% (59.52±8.84% retention), showing that recurrence alone is insufficient in this reduced regime.

Parameter-matched non-recurrent temporal control clean 98.24±0.70%, interpolation 86.67±7.40% (88.25±8.00% retention), dropout 98.24±0.70%; therefore per-step recurrent robustness does not exceed a strong primitive-isolated non-recurrent encoder here.
After a t=50 hidden perturbation, source-like RNN RMS distance fell to 28.91±3.82% of step-1 distance by step30 versus 57.67±11.07% for the final-only recurrent control.
Reduced source-like hidden PR was ~6.76 rather than the paper's ~2.11; low-dimensional ring geometry was not reproduced, so the observed robustness should not be called an attractor-specific effect.
candidate_update.interpretation: The most defensible causal update is that temporal supervision over the whole sequence can sculpt contractive recurrent dynamics and robustness to missing/interpolated frames. The evidence still does not show that the published low-dimensional continuous-attractor geometry itself is necessary or sufficient, because a non-recurrent primitive encoder matched the interpolation retention and exceeded dropout performance, and the reduced recurrent experiment did not reproduce the reported 2D ring.
candidate_update.exact_next_action: Keep trying public metadata/file-list resolution for Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 and non-author rerun/failure evidence. In parallel, run the sharper geometry intervention on the same T=100 generator: add an explicit 2D circular bottleneck/manifold regularizer to the source-equation recurrent model, train a no-manifold recurrent control and a non-recurrent control to matched clean accuracy, then test whether measured PR, off-manifold contraction and random-interpolation/dropout robustness co-vary. If the 2D intervention improves robustness after matching accuracy, follow with a geometry-destroying ablation that preserves readout accuracy; if not, downgrade attractor-specific causality and retain primitive isolation/per-step supervision as the supported mechanism.
